quick: 75 mg/day (IR in 2-3 divided doses); max 225-375 mg/day
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; third-trimester neonatal effects
Excreted in milk; weigh benefit vs risk
summary: Venlafaxine is an SNRI antidepressant used for major depressive disorder. It carries a boxed warning for increased suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults. It can raise blood pressure dose-dependently, requires gradual tapering to avoid a discontinuation syndrome, and is contraindicated with MAO inhibitors due to serotonin syndrome risk.

dosage.d: Start 75 mg/day; may increase to 150 mg/day, then up to 225 mg/day
dosage.t: Two or three divided doses with food
dosage.n: Increase in increments of up to 75 mg/day at intervals of no less than 4 days; max 375 mg/day (in 3 divided doses) for severe inpatients
Withhold dose until completion of hemodialysis
Greater reductions may be needed in more severe cirrhosis

admin: Take with food at approximately the same time(s) each day
Immediate-release tablets given in 2-3 divided doses; extended-release once daily
Swallow extended-release capsules/tablets whole - do not crush, chew, or dissolve
Do not stop abruptly - taper the dose gradually when discontinuing
moa: Venlafaxine and its active metabolite O-desmethylvenlafaxine (ODV) are potent inhibitors of neuronal serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake and weak inhibitors of dopamine reuptake, potentiating monoaminergic neurotransmission in the CNS. They have no significant affinity for muscarinic, histaminergic, or alpha-1 adrenergic receptors and no MAO-inhibitory activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to venlafaxine hydrochloride or any excipient
Concurrent MAO inhibitors for psychiatric disorders, or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI; do not start an MAOI within 7 days of stopping venlafaxine
Concurrent linezolid or intravenous methylene blue
monitor: Suicidality (especially <25 years and early in therapy)

preg: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. Neonates exposed to SNRIs/SSRIs late in the third trimester have developed complications requiring prolonged hospitalization, respiratory support, and tube feeding; there may also be a small increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage.
lact: Venlafaxine and ODV are excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, weighing the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Reduce the total daily dose by 25-50% in renal impairment, and withhold doses until hemodialysis is completed in dialysis patients, as clearance of venlafaxine and ODV is reduced.
hepatic: Reduce the total daily dose by about 50% in hepatic impairment; greater reductions may be necessary in more severe cirrhosis because clearance is decreased and exposure increased.

major: MAO inhibitors (serotonin syndrome / hypertensive crisis - contraindicated)
Linezolid and intravenous methylene blue (serotonin syndrome)
Other serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, triptans, tramadol, lithium, St. John's wort)
moderate: Diuretics and other drugs causing hyponatremia
minor: Drugs that lower the seizure threshold
interactions.food: Take with food; food does not significantly affect bioavailability but improves tolerability
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor blood pressure and serum sodium; may affect bleeding parameters

monitoring: Suicidality and mood, especially early and after dose changes
Blood pressure at baseline and periodically (increase risk with higher doses)
Signs of serotonin syndrome and abnormal bleeding
Heart rate and ECG where cardiac risk exists
counsel: Full antidepressant benefit may take several weeks
Do not stop suddenly - taper to avoid withdrawal (dizziness, nausea, headache, electric-shock sensations, irritability)
Report worsening mood, agitation, or thoughts of self-harm immediately
Avoid alcohol and tell your prescriber about all serotonergic medicines
pk: Antidepressant benefit develops over several weeks
IR dosed 2-3 times daily; XR supports once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F) in a dry place
pearls: Boxed warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults - monitor closely early in therapy
Causes dose-dependent sustained hypertension - check blood pressure regularly
Notorious for a discontinuation syndrome; always taper gradually
Active metabolite ODV (desvenlafaxine) carries most of the activity and a longer half-life
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause somnolence, tachycardia, ECG changes (QT prolongation, bundle branch block, QRS widening), seizures, serotonin syndrome, altered consciousness, and rarely coma; fatalities have occurred, especially with mixed ingestions including alcohol or other drugs. Management is supportive with airway protection, cardiac monitoring, and seizure/serotonin-syndrome treatment; activated charcoal may help if given early. Forced diuresis, dialysis, hemoperfusion, and exchange transfusion are unlikely to be beneficial. No specific antidote.
